era_note: Baltimore, 26 March 2024, forward to the NTSB board meeting of 18 November 2025 and the indictment unsealed 12 May 2026. THIS IS A LIVE CRIMINAL CASE. Per episode_spec forbidden_claims, no Short says Synergy Marine, Synergy Maritime or Nair caused the collapse (charged, not convicted), that anyone lied to the NTSB, that the proper pumps would have cleared the bridge (that is the indictment's allegation and must be spoken as one), that the civil settlement admitted anything, or that Maryland knew the bridge was vulnerable (the Board found them likely unaware). No length in feet for the Dali is stated as fact where the record gives three different figures - the 947 figure appears only inside the script's own sentence. Per forbidden_subjects, no body, no victim, no collision, no bridge collapsing, no child, and no non-US place names.
plate_pool_note: 131 plates on disk at remotion/public/keybridge/img, each with a matching _depth.png. Subjects from the episode's own Codex plate table: the night road crew H003-H011, the ship and her machinery H012-H044, the breakers and the wire H065-H072, the hearing and the courthouse H076-H096, the bridges that remain H104-H119. Every plate below verified present; no plate is used by more than one Short.

shorts.angle: Everyone on the water did the right thing in the right order - closed the breakers by hand twice, called the tug, warned the channel, stopped the traffic - and the recorder proves it. Sixty-seven seconds still ran out.
shorts.avoids: Names no defendant and no company; makes no claim about why the ship failed to recover, which is the contested part. Does not depict the collision, the collapse or the six men beyond the script's own sentence that they were gone. No allegation is spoken at all in this Short.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: If nobody on that ship made a mistake, what was it that kept switching the power off?
shorts.loop_join: The close asks how the seconds ran out; the hook is the order given with sixty-seven of them left.

lines.text: At twenty-seven minutes and fifty-three seconds past one in the morning, a duty officer in Baltimore gave an order to stop the traffic.
source_lines: At twenty-seven minutes and fifty-three seconds past one in the morning, a duty officer in Baltimore gave an order to stop the traffic.

lines.text: Sixty-seven seconds later the bridge was in the river, and six men who had been filling potholes on it were gone.
source_lines: Sixty-seven seconds later the bridge was in the river, and six men who had been filling potholes on it were gone.

lines.text: Everyone who could act, acted. So how did the sixty-seven seconds run out?
source_lines: Everyone who could act, acted.
So how did the sixty-seven seconds run out?

lines.text: The engineers found the breakers and closed them by hand — twice, under a blackout, at night, in a channel.
source_lines: The engineers found the breakers and closed them by hand — twice, under a blackout, at night, in a channel.

lines.text: The pilots called for a tug within seventy-four seconds of the first blackout. A pilot broadcast a warning to everything floating in the Patapsco. The duty officer stopped the traffic.
source_lines: The pilots called for a tug within seventy-four seconds of the first blackout.
A pilot broadcast a warning to everything floating in the Patapsco.
The duty officer stopped the traffic.

lines.text: The tug was three miles out. The bridge was two tenths of a mile ahead. Nobody was going to close that gap.
source_lines: The tug was three miles out.
The bridge was two tenths of a mile ahead.
Nobody was going to close that gap.

lines.text: There is a recording of four minutes in which a professional crew did the right things in the right order and it did not matter.
source_lines: There is a recording of four minutes in which a professional crew did the right things in the right order and it did not matter.

lines.text: There is no moment on that tape where somebody freezes, or argues, or fails to understand what is happening.
source_lines: There is no moment on that tape where somebody freezes, or argues, or fails to understand what is happening.

shorts.angle: The National Transportation Safety Board took twenty months to name the probable cause, and it is a label band that held one wire a fraction of a millimetre short of its clamp.
shorts.avoids: States the Board's probable cause and nothing beyond it. Does not touch the indictment, the flushing pump, the companies or Nair - the contested second half belongs to the long-form. No allegation, no blame, no victim, no collision.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: The wire explains the first blackout. Why did a ship built to restart itself not come back?
shorts.loop_join: The close - the physical cause is a label in the wrong place - is the hook's twenty months, answered.

lines.text: It took the National Transportation Safety Board twenty months to say why. It was a wire.
source_lines: It took the National Transportation Safety Board twenty months to say why.
It was a wire.

lines.text: On the eighteenth of November, 2025, the Board met and determined the probable cause.
source_lines: On the eighteenth of November, 2025, the Board met and determined the probable cause.

lines.text: A loose signal wire connection to a terminal block, stemming from the improper installation of wire-label banding, which caused the loss of electrical power, which caused the loss of propulsion and steering close to the bridge.
source_lines: Specifically: a loose signal wire connection to a terminal block, stemming from the improper installation of wire-label banding, which caused the loss of electrical power, which caused the loss of propulsion and steering close to the bridge.

lines.text: The mechanism is small enough to hold between two fingers. A terminal block has a spring-clamp gate that grips a wire.
source_lines: The mechanism is small enough to hold between two fingers.
A terminal block has a spring-clamp gate that grips a wire.

lines.text: Somebody had put a band of labelling around that wire. The band stopped the wire seating fully into the gate. The connection was inadequate.
source_lines: Somebody had put a band of labelling around that wire.
The band stopped the wire seating fully into the gate.
The connection was inadequate.

lines.text: That is the whole thing.
source_lines: That is the whole thing.

lines.text: A ship of this size, a bridge of this size, six men, and the physical cause is a label that was a fraction of a millimetre too thick in the wrong place.
source_lines: A ship of this size, a bridge of this size, six men, and the physical cause is a label that was a fraction of a millimetre too thick in the wrong place.

lines.text: But that explains the first blackout. It does not explain why she did not come back.
source_lines: But that explains the first blackout.
It does not explain why she did not come back.

shorts.angle: The Board's quieter finding: the bridge had no countermeasures against a modern ship, the owner was likely unaware the risk applied to them, and sixty-eight other American bridges have never had the sum done.
shorts.avoids: Does not say Maryland knew and ignored the guidance - it states the Board's own finding that they were likely unaware. Does not say the sixty-eight bridges are unsafe; the script's own qualification is spoken. Names no defendant, states no allegation, shows no collapse.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: Who is supposed to do that arithmetic for the bridge you drove over this morning?
shorts.loop_join: The close - somebody's commute - returns to the hook's bridge standing over a shipping channel tonight.

lines.text: A bridge stays exactly where it is while the ships underneath it keep getting bigger.
source_lines: And a bridge stays exactly where it is while the ships underneath it keep getting bigger.

lines.text: Contributing to the collapse was the absence of countermeasures to reduce the bridge's vulnerability to being struck by an ocean-going vessel.
source_lines: Contributing to the collapse and to the loss of life was the absence of countermeasures to reduce the bridge's vulnerability to being struck by an ocean-going vessel — countermeasures that could have been put in place if the Maryland Transportation Authority had carried out a vulnerability assessment.

lines.text: It did not find that Maryland knew and ignored it. It found that they were likely unaware of the potential risk. Not a cover-up.
source_lines: It did not find that Maryland knew and ignored it.
It found that they were likely unaware of the potential risk.
Not a cover-up.

lines.text: A vulnerability assessment sounds like a filing cabinet. It is a sum. Take the bridge you have.
source_lines: A vulnerability assessment sounds like a filing cabinet.
It is a sum.
Take the bridge you have.

lines.text: Take the ships that use the channel now, not the ships that used it when the bridge was drawn. Then find out whether the protection you already have is protection. Or decoration.
source_lines: Take the ships that use the channel now, not the ships that used it when the bridge was drawn.
Then find out whether the protection you already have is protection.
Or decoration.

lines.text: That is the failure. Not neglect. Arithmetic that went quietly out of date.
source_lines: That is the failure.
Not neglect.
Arithmetic that went quietly out of date.

lines.text: Sixty-eight. Sixty-eight bridges in the United States for which the NTSB recommended a vulnerability evaluation.
source_lines: Sixty-eight.
Sixty-eight bridges in the United States for which the NTSB recommended a vulnerability evaluation.

lines.text: Not sixty-eight bridges that are unsafe. Sixty-eight bridges where nobody had done the arithmetic, because the question had never been asked in that form. Every one of those is somebody's commute.
source_lines: Not sixty-eight bridges that are unsafe.
Sixty-eight bridges where nobody had done the arithmetic — where the owner could not say what would happen if a modern ship hit a pier, because the question had never been asked in that form.
Every one of those is somebody's commute.
